newsitem.title: CHINA: Moderate earthquake rocks western China region.
newsitem.headline: Moderate earthquake rocks western China region.

text.p: An earthquake measuring 6.4 on the Richter scale rocked a farming area of China's westernmost Xinjiang region on Tuesday, causing some casualties, officials said.
"There were definitely some people injured and possibly deaths," said a local official reached by telephone in Jiashi, about 50 km (30 miles) from the bazaar town of Kashgar.
"But it is still too early to say how many," he said, adding that local officials were checking the extent of damage in an area with a fairly large population of sheep farmers.
The earthquake of 6.4 magnitude, which can cause widespread damage, struck the farming district of Jiashi at 9.47 a.m. (0147 GMT), state television said.
An unknown number of houses had collapsed and cracks had appeared in others, it quoted local officials as saying.
"It felt much stronger than last time," the local official said, referring to an earthquake of 6.9 magnitude that rocked Jiashi in March last year, killing 26 people and injuring 128.
A special task force had been organised to check on damage throughout the district and to help with relief work, state television said. It gave no more details.
A tremor measuring 5.0 on the open-ended Richter scale shook a remote corner of China's Tibet region on Monday.

The quake was centred in the Naqu region, about 600 km (360 miles) northwest of the regional capital, Lhasa. There were no immediate reports of injuries or damage and the mountainous region is thinly populated.
